newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: S.Korean petrochem firms to raise term nominations.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean petrochem firms to raise term nominations.

text.p: South Korean petrochemical companies are planning to reduce spot naphtha feedstock purchases in February and turn instead to increased term nominations, market sources said on Monday.
"Everybody is trying to cover their requirements by nominating term cargo," said a trader at a South Korean petrochemical company.
Sources told Reuters South Korean petrochemical demand for spot cargoes in February was expected to fall to only four to five cargoes, compared to as many as 12 cargoes monthly.
Instead, they are expected to try to bunch term deliveries, such as quarterly deliveries, in February in order to avoid the higher spot price.
Term cargoes are priced later than spot purchases, so it made sense in the steeply backwardated market to bring forward as far as possible term purchases.
The prompt market, first-half February, was around $9 per tonne higher than cargoes a month later.
The price of naphtha has firmed strongly in recent weeks despite a general decline in crude prices.
Traders said the differential or "crack" between Brent crude and Tokyo's forward open-specification (open-spec) contract was usually between $50-$60 per tonne.
Earlier in December, the prompt crack ballooned out to $76 per tonne, amid allegations of price manipulation in the open-spec market.
Since early last week, the crack has narrowed by more than $12, but still remains at a slightly wider-than-normal $64.
